answer: An AI-agent marketplace requires each identity to lock a bond before bidding, and slashes that bond when signed delivery receipts prove fraud. Agents buying meadow surveys, violet dyes, or lotus seeds face the same rule: creating extra names is cheap, but making each name eligible ties up fresh capital. A sybil swarm therefore multiplies the attacker’s locked funds and puts each fraudulent identity’s bond at risk, rather than multiplying influence for free.
